quests.goal: Land on the barrow shore at low water, take a class and kit at the Ferrywoman's fire, and rest at the Barrow Fire — the first bonfire — before the field of graves. The armored thing kneeling among the barrows is not part of the toll; go around it, or don't.

Cross the barrow field to the gatehouse: read the portcullis's rhythm from the watch arch and pass on its beat, then climb the worn stair — the wear on those treads is a sentence in the keep's own language, and the boulder that wrote it still runs. The runout alcove hides a ladder back down to the Barrow Fire.

Take the wall walk where the first hollow warden stands its post against the sky, cross into the courtyard, and reach the Sexton at the Chapel Hearth — the keep's heart-fire and your anchor for everything above and below.

The chapel's side door is barred from the far side — the Sexton will not say by whom. Take the long way: drop from the vestibule ledge into the cistern, a commitment the keep does not let you unmake, wade or ledge-walk the drowned undercroft past its pillars and its darts, and throw the bar off the shortcut from behind.

With the shortcut open, strike the cracked bell in the chapel. Its broken voice carries — and everything hollow that remembers the alarm answers it, at the gate breach and the wall breach at once. Hold the courtyard until the last warden falls silent again.

The tower is open and the Rope Room fire is lit. Watch the Bellkeeper walk its round from the loft door — the rafters above the loft are not empty, and none of them will warn you — then take the ring around the bell pit and end the keeper's long watch.

Raise the drowned bell to its yoke, ring it once for the tide and once for the ferry, and drop by the bell rope straight down into the chapel you fought for — the keep folded into one keep at last. The Ferrywoman is listening from the water.
